title: Mewgenics
genre: Turn-based grid tactics roguelike + cat-breeding / genetics 'legacy' sim
release_date: 2026-02-10 (Steam, PC; global launch 9 AM PST) [CONFIRMED – Tyler Glaiel on Reddit via Prima Games; RPG Site]; consoles (PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2): announced at gamescom Opening Night Live 2026 for 2026-09-08, published by Nicalis [CONFIRMED – announcement via Siliconera/Wikipedia; launch-day coverage not found]
developer: Edmund McMillen & Tyler Glaiel (credited as individuals; no separate studio brand found)
team_size: 2 core developers (McMillen – design/art; Glaiel – programming/design) + background artist Krystal Fleming + music by Ridiculon (Matthias Bossi, Jon Evans) [CONFIRMED – McMillen's announced team via Wikipedia/Giant Bomb]; plus 'some handpicked devs from their community' [Rhys Elliott/Alinea on X]. Exact headcount: no data.
country: no data (not stated in sources retrieved)
developer_background: Mewgenics was first announced by Team Meat in 2012 as the follow-up to Super Meat Boy (playable at PAX Prime 2013 / PAX East 2014), then shelved (Feb 2016) amid differing priorities between Team Meat co-owners McMillen and Tommy Refenes. In Jan 2018 McMillen announced he had acquired the rights and would work full-time with Tyler Glaiel, his collaborator on The End Is Nigh; Refenes 'not at all' involved. Glaiel tested brawler and RTS prototypes before settling on turn-based grid tactics; the game was rebuilt from scratch except the original soundtrack [CONFIRMED – McMillen statements reported by Game Informer (2018) and summarised by Wikipedia/Giant Bomb]. Ridiculon also scored The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth.
publisher: PC: self-published (Edmund McMillen, Tyler Glaiel); consoles: Nicalis [CONFIRMED – Wikipedia infobox; eShop/Microsoft Store listings via Siliconera]
platforms_and_store_links: Steam (PC): https://store.steampowered.com/app/686060/Mewgenics/ (Steam Deck compatible at launch – GamingOnLinux); no GOG/Epic at launch (Prima Games); PS5 / Xbox Series X|S / Switch 2 via Nicalis, dated 2026-09-08 (Siliconera, RPG Site).
business_model: premium $29.99 (10% launch discount until 2026-02-24); Steam regional pricing follows Valve's recommendations; consoles reportedly $39.99 (single Dutch outlet – unverified)
price_usd: $29.99 [CONFIRMED – Steam store price via Game8/RPG Site/steamdata.ai]
units_or_downloads: 150,000 within ~6 hours (AllKeyShop report); 250,000 in <12 hours; 500,000 in ~36 hours; 1,000,000 by 2026-02-17 (~7 days) [CONFIRMED – Tyler Glaiel social posts via PC Gamer, Game Informer, Game Developer, Rogueliker]. No later official milestone found (searched for 2M/3M). Steam total by ~2026-09-05: ~2.4M (range 2.1M–2.7M) [ESTIMATE – 53,457 reviews × 45 (the game's own implied launch ratio; range ×40–50)]. Trackers: Raijin ~2.9M (2026-09-05, medium confidence), VG Insights ~2.2M (undated). Console units (from 2026-09-08): no data.
peak_concurrent_players: 115,428 on 2026-02-15 [CONFIRMED – Steam data via SteamDB, reported by Rogueliker/Tbreak/Notebookcheck]; above Hades II's 112,947 (Sept 2025). 65,962 peak in first 24 hours. Tracker.gg lists 115,398. Later: ~5,700 live / ~6,300 24h peak at an undated 2026 tracker.gg snapshot [ESTIMATE – tracker].
steam_reviews: 53,457 reviews, 90% positive (~2026-09-05, Raijin); ~55.5k 'Very Positive' (steamdata.ai, slightly later snapshot); launch week: 22,189 reviews with 1,626 negative (~92%) around 2026-02-17 (KitGuru/Rogueliker). Metacritic 89 (Game Informer).
implied_review_multiplier: ~45 (1,000,000 confirmed copies on 2026-02-17 ÷ ~22,189 reviews at the same time)
gross_revenue: Steam: ~$54M by ~Sep 2026 (range $48M–$60M) [ESTIMATE – 2.4M units (2.1–2.7M) × $22.49 avg realised price ($29.99 × 0.75)]. Tracker estimates: Raijin $52.3M lifetime (Aug/Sep 2026; was $48.2M in Mar 2026), VG Insights $48.6M. Launch week: ~$23–25M at 1M copies [ESTIMATE – Alinea Analytics via GameSpot/Notebookcheck].
net_revenue: Steam: ~$37.5M (range $33M–$42M) [ESTIMATE – Steam 30% on first $10M, 25% on $10M–$50M, 20% above; × 0.93 refunds]. PC is self-published, so no publisher split; console revenue goes through Nicalis (split not disclosed).
production_cost: ~$1.0M–$1.6M [ESTIMATE – ~2–3 FTE (Glaiel full-time from May 2019, McMillen, background artist) × ~81 months (May 2019–Feb 2026) × $6k/mo, plus contracted music]. Cross-check: Glaiel said the game recouped its development costs within ~3 hours of launch [CONFIRMED – Glaiel via PC Gamer/mezha/itc.ua]; AllKeyShop's own unofficial budget guess was ~$1.4M.
development_time: ~6.75 years for the shipped version (Glaiel full-time from May 2019, starting with a new engine → 2026-02-10); rights reacquired Jan 2018; ~14 years since the 2012 Team Meat announcement [CONFIRMED dates via Wikipedia/Giant Bomb; durations computed]. Steam page went live Oct 2022.
why_popular: Decade-long cult anticipation for a 'lost' McMillen project; very deep, replayable tactics roguelike where breeding and genetic inheritance create personal, emergent stories about individual cats; grotesque-cute humour that is highly shareable; strong pre-launch reviews (Metacritic 89) converted wishlists (~400k before reviews → ~600k at launch) [CONFIRMED – Glaiel via PC Gamer]. Sales far exceeded what wishlists predicted ('we both got a bit blindsided').
marketing_channels: Creator fame and existing fan community (Super Meat Boy/Isaac audience, Reddit, Discord); long Steam wishlist build since 2022; review embargo lifted before launch (≈+200k wishlists); streamers/YouTubers; devs posting live sales milestones on social media, which became press stories; Steam top-seller/most-played momentum; Steam Deck verified at launch; console ports announced at gamescom ONL 2026.
engine: Custom engine written by Tyler Glaiel (work on a new engine began May 2019) [ESTIMATE – secondary sources: Giant Bomb wiki, Wikipedia, lorcana.gg; no direct developer quote retrieved]
art_style: Edmund McMillen's hand-drawn 2D cartoon style: grotesque-cute cats, gross-out humour, flat colours, puppet-style 2D animation.
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: code grid-tactics combat, the roguelike run structure, a breeding/inheritance data model and save system; generate placeholder 2D art and many ability icons; draft ability/item text; SFX and music. AI cannot: design hundreds of interacting abilities, mutations and classes that stay balanced; McMillen's distinctive art voice and humour; years of playtest-driven tuning; an existing million-strong fan base. Something 'similar in spirit' (a small tactics roguelike with a breeding meta-layer) is doable solo; matching Mewgenics' depth would take years. | Toolset: Claude Code + Godot 4 (or Unity) + GodotSteam/Steamworks.NET, Retro Diffusion/Scenario/Midjourney for 2D concepts and sprites (heavy manual clean-up), Spine or Godot 2D skeletal animation, ElevenLabs SFX, Suno/Udio music, spreadsheet-driven balance data.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 8–12 weeks, ~$500–$1,500 (Claude Max $100–$200/mo, image gen $30–$60/mo, audio ~$30/mo, Steam Direct $100). Excludes developer living costs.
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 12–24 months, ~$8,000–$30,000 (tools ~$300/mo, freelance 2D art/animation for a coherent style $3k–$15k, music $1k–$5k, playtests/marketing $1k–$5k). Excludes developer living costs.

data_conflicts: Steam units: Raijin ~2.9M vs VG Insights ~2.2M; chose ~2.4M from the game's own calibrated ratio (×45), roughly midway. Peak CCU 115,428 (SteamDB via press) vs 115,398 (tracker.gg). Press called it the 'most-played roguelite in Steam history' (beating Hades II), but Megabonk peaked higher (117,336, Oct 2025), so that claim depends on genre definition. Launch-week gross: Alinea $23M–$25M vs this spec's method ~$22.5M. Shelving date: Aug 2014 'on hold' vs Feb 2016 'shelved' (Wikipedia vs Giant Bomb). Console launch on 2026-09-08 is listed by Wikipedia, but no launch-day coverage was found. The $39.99 console price comes from one minor outlet. Engine is 'custom' only per secondary sources.
notes: Biggest premium indie launch of early 2026 by speed (1M in a week at $29.99). For solo creators: (1) 'systems that generate personal stories' (breeding/inheritance) are a strong hook; (2) review embargo before launch can add ~50% to wishlists; (3) posting live milestones creates free press. Steam-only at launch; consoles came ~7 months later through a publisher (Nicalis).
